claims.text: Specifically, Judge Amit Mehta ruled on August 5, 2024 that Google was a monopolist in general search services and general search text advertising [Source: ev-1].

claims.text: The theory of harm centered on Google paying companies like Apple, Samsung, and Mozilla billions to be their default search engine; evidence showed Google paid approximately $26.3 billion for distribution in 2021 and paid Apple roughly 36% of Safari search-ad revenue [Source: ev-1].
This practice created a self-reinforcing loop where defaults led to scale, data, quality, and protection of the default position, which rivals could not break [Source: ev-1].

The remedies ordered by Judge Mehta on August 5, 2035 (noted as 2025 in the text) included structural measures requiring Google to sell Chrome, marking the first forced divestiture of a major tech company since the Microsoft case of 2000 [Source: ev-1].
